newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions -Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions -Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, October 14 - Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 1 discharging/loading containers, 1 loading bananas, 1 discharging corn, 1 discharging soya, 1 discharging paper products. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 to load lumber products, 1 awaiting instructions. 14 Vessels due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas, 1 to load zinc concentrates, no berthing delays expected. Vessels berthed, 2 discharging/loading containers, 2 discharging bulk corn, 1 loading bananas, 1 discharging generals. Vessels awaiting berth, 3 for discharging/loading containers, 1 for loading bananas, 1 for discharging/loading generals, 1 for discharging grain. Vessels due, 5 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load generals, 3 to load bananas, 1 to discharge wheat, 1 to discharge fertiliser.

PANAMA, October 11 - Panama Canal - Canal traffic situation is now almost normal with a total of 30 vessels awaiting transit as at midnight 10/11. Whilst there are not major lane outages programmed until next march, there will be surges of traffic when the use of the transit booking system may have to be considered. Balboa - Vessels in port, 1 bulk, 1 car carrier. Cristobal - Vessels in port, 2 general cargo/containers, 1 reefer, 1 bulk. Panama Canal - Traffic moving normally, 39 vessels due, 23 in queue, 7 booked, 40 scheduled. On 14/10 arrivals were 38, transits 39, average canal waiting time 18.2 hours. Rain. Cruise vessel alongside, 3 container vessels alongside, 2 tankers loading, 3 tugs and barges alongside. Offport anchorage - 2 Vessels at anchor for bunkering. Barbers Point, HI - Harbour - 1 Tug and barge alongside, 1 tanker alongside loading. Offport anchorage - 1 Tanker discharging crude. Columbia River - Congestion is mild at the Columbia River. Grain vessels will experience up to 3 days berthing delay. Astoria - 1 Grain vessel anchored. Portland - 1 Grain vessel anchored, 1 grain vessel at layberth, 4 grain vessels loading. 2 Vessels under repair, 2 container vessels alongside, 1 cement vessel discharging, 1 tanker discharging, 1 vessel discharging alumina, 1 vessel loading soda ash, 1 vessel discharging autos. Vancouver, WA - One vessel loading grain. Kalama - One vessel loading grain. Longview - Two vessels loading logs, 1 loading potash, 1 loading lumber.

October 15 - Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating, 7 bulkers, 3 container vessels, 1 ro/ro, 2 auto vessels, 3 tankers, 3 general cargo, 2 cable vessels on standby. 3 Vessels in repair yard, 4 bulkers awaiting berth of which 2 to discharge sugar, 1 to discharge ore, 1 other vessel. East Coast - Baltimore, MD - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week. No adverse conditions at c/d canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well, with no delays. Average waiting time for consol coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage cleat at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - Light to moderate traffic in Columbus Street terminal during the coming week. Moderate to heavy cargo operations at the Wando terminal. No delays at the oil facilities. No delays expected for cargo operations or vessel movement.

Jacksonville - Heavy berth congestion or delays at Jacksonville and Fernandina Beach, FL. Miami, FL - No congestion at container berths. Ro/ro berths available. Passenger terminals will be available from 0600 hours to 1900 hours Tuesday to Thursday and Friday to Monday. Terminals will be fully operational. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container, tanker terminals. Congestion continues at Brooklyn sugar terminal and at Yonkers sugar terminal. Norfolk, VA - Twelve vessels due at Norfolk Souern coal pier. 3 Vessels anchored waiting to load. 12 Vessels due at Dominion terminal, 7 anchored waiting to load. 3 Vessels due at Pier IX coal terminal.

Scheduled maintenance at Norfolk Southern began 1/10. Completion expected by 19/10. During this period, one loader will be in operation. One vessel due at Cargill during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals working normally, with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are working normally. All channels are opening with prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in the port, nor at Camden, Wilmington. No navigational problems. Savannah, GA - No congestion expected at the Georgia ports authorities Garden City terminal for the coming week. Moderate congestion expected at the Ocean terminal. All liquid bulk facilities are operating normally. No berth congestion expected. One to two days delay expected at the Colonial Marine terminal for bulk clay.

Due to afternoon thunder showers, vessels with weather sensitive cargo may expect some downtime. Some delays may be expected due to periods of fog in the early morning hours. All navigational conditions remain normal. The port of Savannah suffered no ill effects from tropical storm Josephine. The captain of the port closed the Savannah River to all deep draft traffic on 7/10, and was reopened early on 8/10. Gulf coast - Houston, TX - City docks congested as approx. 15 ships are scheduled to berth 15/10. No congestion at private terminals. Chemical docks and grain elevators at Houston, Galveston. Mobile, AL - Both private and state-owned facilities continue to operate normally.

New Orleans, LA - Rain causes delays in cargo operations, especially grain loading. River stage at 5.3 feet, normal transit times can be expected. Bar pilots advise that on 19/10 and 20/10, the draft for the Mississippi River gulf outlet will be 30 ft. Present max. permissible draft at Southwest Pass is 47 ft. FW for vessels under 100,000 dwt. Some elevators are now working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments. West coast - Columbia River - Wheat export has slowed down due to lack of product. Currently 8 grain vessels in the district of which 6 loading, 2 waiting with average waiting time of 1-3 days. Coos Bay - Vessels in port, 2 linerboard and various lumber and log vessels, some berthing delays expected. Three woodchip vessels at Roseburg dock, 1 at GB. Glenbrook nickel - 1 Ore vessel operating, 1 due next week.

Long Beach - Metropolitan - Moderately heavy for October, 2-3 days delay awaiting berth expected. Koch Carbon - 3 Vessels due this month. Kaiser - Moderately heavy for October, 2-3 days berthing delay expected for coal/petcoke. October moderately heavy in the Los Angeles/Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes. Fog has caused delays of 2-4 hours for vessels berthing/sailing. This situation is expected to continue for the next 1-2 weeks. San Francisco, CA - No congestion at the tanker terminal at present. Seattle - Grain vessel activity is increasing.
